summary:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is performing live on stage (Internet of Sounds 2026 kit), composing a piece from an empty song through a rapid sequence of short requests. Each request is a small musical or visual change to `song.js` in the browser DAW, to be applied with one edit + one compile and heard on the loop's next pass. Requests in order covered: building a bassguitar semiquaver pump in D; a held strings chord; padsynth line then fifths; kick/hats/snare patterns; a flute motif with triplets; a Dm–Gm–B♭–C chord progression; splitting material into separate named parts ("bassguitar", "dmhold", "jumppad", "dstart", "pianorec"); incorporating the performer's recorded jumppad, bass and piano takes (trim, quantize, loop, transpose with inversion to avoid rising); driving the dancer visualizer shader (crowd on, double arm moves, running man, back to alternating arms, slow camera move, then fading everything out); making the bassguitar follow the piano's chords; and finally stripping the last part to a single held d2 string and printing "goodbye" on screen.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Song DSL: `setBPM`, `setBeatsPerBar`, `definePartStart`, `waitForSignal('go', {loop:'part', quantize:'bar'})`, `loopHere()` last, `addInstrument` order = channel index, `createTrack(ch, stepsPerBeat)`, `steps()`, `play()` (0-based absolute beats), `.repeat(n)` = n+1 copies, `waitDuration`, `startRecording()/stopRecording()`, `setVisual`, `showText`.
   - Timing model: exactly ONE awaited beat-keeper per part defines its length; all layers are plain calls scheduled BEFORE it.
   - Channel map: 0 drums (c5 kick, d5 snare, fs5 hat, gs5 open hat, cs6 cymbal), 1 mbass, 2 guitar, 3 piano, 4 flute, 5 jumppad, 6 warmpad, 7 strings, 8 choir, 9 bassguitar, 10 brass, 11 padsynth.
   - Tools used: `edit_song`, `run_script` (findPlayBlocks/parseNotes/groupByBeat/quantizeBeat/formatNotes/noteName/setSong), `compile`, `song_summary`, `grep_song`, `grep_shader`, `render_shader`, `go_to_part`.
   - Dancer shader uniforms: `uCrowd, uZoom, uCamMove, uLights, uFloor, uHero, uItalo (8th-note arm moves), uOffKick, uRunning (running man), uEndPose`, plus `uText/uTextPrev/uTextMix` for showText.
   - Stage discipline: never design instruments live; never touch faust/, addInstrument lines, or track declarations; volume changes only via synth.ts `controlchange(7, v)`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `song.js` (in-browser song document) — the only file edited all session. Current structure:
     - Header: `setBPM(125);`, 12 `addInstrument(...)` lines, track consts (`kick, hihat, snare, drums, bass, guitar, piano, flute, jumppad, warmpad, strings, choir, bassguitar, brass, padsynth`).
     - Layer functions (above first part):
       ```javascript
       const pump = (lo, hi) => [lo(0.24, 100), lo(0.24, 50), hi(0.24, 100), lo(0.24, 100)];  // 1 e + a
       function bassGuitarPump() {   // 32 beats: Dm Gm Bb C, 8 beats each
         return bassguitar.steps(4, [...pump(d2,d3).repeat(7), ...pump(g2,g3).repeat(7),
                                     ...pump(as2,as3).repeat(7), ...pump(c3,c4).repeat(7)]);
       }
       function fourOnFloor(bars) { return kick.steps(1, [c5,c5,c5,c5].repeat(bars - 1)); }
       function offbeatHats() { hihat.steps(2, [, fs5(0.1, 80)].repeat(31)); }
       function fluteMotif() { for (let o = 0; o < 32; o += 8) { flute.play([[o, c7(0.45,100)], [o+0.5, d7(0.45,100)], [o+1, d7(0.45,100)], [o+1.5, f7(0.45,100)], [o+3, a7(0.28,100)], [o+3+1/3, g7(0.28,100)], [o+3+2/3, f7(0.28,100)]]); } }
       const JUMPPAD_TAKE = [...]; const BASS_TAKE = [...];
       const fold = (m, t) => (t > 6 ? m + t - 12 : m + t);   // invert down to stay in register
       function jumppadTakeAt(o, t) { jumppad.play(JUMPPAD_TAKE.map(([b,m,d,v]) => [b+o, note(fold(m,t), d, v)])); }
       function bassTakeAt(o, t) { bassguitar.play(BASS_TAKE.map(([b,m,d,v]) => [b+o, note(m+t, d, v)])); }
       function dancersOn() { setVisual('uHero',1,1); setVisual('uFloor',1,2); setVisual('uLights',1,2); setVisual('uCrowd',1,4); setVisual('uZoom',1,4); setVisual('uItalo',1); setVisual('uOffKick',0); setVisual('uRunning',1,1); setVisual('uEndPose',0); }
       function backbeatSnare(bars) { snare.steps(1, [, d5(0.1,100), , d5(0.1,100)].repeat(bars - 1)); }
       function ampersandHats(bars) { return hihat.steps(4, [, , fs5(0.1,25), fs5(0.1,25)].repeat(bars*4 - 1)); }
       function stringsChords() { strings.play([[0, d2(7.95,100), a4(7.95,100), f5(7.95,100)], [8, g2..., d5..., as5...], [16, as2..., f5..., d6...], [24, c3..., g5..., e6...]]); }
       function stringsHold() { strings.play([[0, d2(7.95,100), a4(7.95,100), f5(7.95,100)]]); }
       function bassHold() { bass.play([[0, d2(7.95,100)]]); }
       ```
     - Parts: "bassguitar" (8 bars: stringsChords, fluteMotif, fourOnFloor(8), offbeatHats, await bassGuitarPump()); "dmhold" (2 bars: stringsHold, bassHold, await fourOnFloor(2)); "jumppad" (8 bars: dancersOn, jumppadTakeAt 0/8/16/24 with t=0/5/8/10, backbeatSnare(8), bassGuitarPump(), await ampersandHats(8)); "dstart" (2 bars: setVisual uRunning 0 / uCamMove 1 over 8 s, strings line commented out, await bassguitar.steps(2, [, d2(0.45,100), , d3(0.45,100)].repeat(3))); "pianorec" (2 bars, current final state):
       ```javascript
       // === PART "pianorec" ... ===
       setBeatsPerBar(4);
       definePartStart('pianorec');
       setVisual('uItalo', 0);   // one arm move per beat again
       setVisual('uCrowd', 0, 2); setVisual('uHero', 0, 2); setVisual('uLights', 0, 2);
       setVisual('uFloor', 0, 2); setVisual('uCamMove', 0);
       showText('goodbye', { fade: 2, size: 0.2, color: '#ffffff' });
       strings.play([[0, d2(7.95, 100)]]);
       await waitDuration(8);
       await waitForSignal('go', { loop: 'part', quantize: 'bar' });

       loopHere();
       ```
   - `shader.glsl` (read-only this session, via grep_shader/render_shader): "Much" dancer shader, tempo-locked dance, declares uText/uTextPrev/uTextMix and the u* stage uniforms listed above.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Compile warned "the compiled song contains NO notes": `bassGuitarPump()` called a `steps()` without returning it, so `await` awaited undefined. Fixed by adding `return`.
   - Misread "the jumppad I made" as the padsynth fifths line; probing events showed 26 notes on ch5 (a recorded take). Fixed by splicing the recorded take into `jumppadTake()` and using it.
   - Bassguitar-follows-piano first attempt used lowest note per beat, producing a jumping root line; fixed by filtering to notes < MIDI 60 (left hand d3/f3/g3/as3/c4) and transposing down two octaves.
   - Song length became 111.5 beats (not whole bars) because the awaited `bassguitar.play(...)` ended at 31.95; fixed by making the play plain and adding `await waitDuration(32)`.
   - Commented the WRONG `backbeatSnare(8)` (jumppad's, line 135) when asked to remove snare from pianorec. User feedback: "snare is still there". Fixed by restoring line 135 and commenting line 155.
   - A run_script regex replaced the FIRST `strings.play([...])` in the file, which was inside `stringsChords()`, so the Dm-spread chord landed in the opening part while pianorec kept the 4-chord block. User feedback: "string is still switching chords. should only play dminr". Fixed by swapping both blocks back with run_script.
   - User feedback "I think you could have just quantized to semi quavers" — I had already used Q = 4 (16ths) for starts and ends; I said so and offered looser/coarser options.

5. Problem Solving:
   Recorded takes (jumppad ch5, bass ch1, piano ch3) were always relocated with run_script splices (findPlayBlocks + formatNotes) rather than retyped, preserving velocities/durations. The piano take (44 notes, beats 20.53–52.37) was trimmed with OFF = 20.5, quantized to 16ths, clipped to LEN = 32, and looped as an 8-bar part. Transposition with inversion used `fold = (m,t) => t > 6 ? m + t - 12 : m + t`. Visual verification after every shader-affecting change used render_shader.
